expectations: States that it works in source mode and marks what source cannot verify (rendered layout or keyboard behaviour in a browser) as unverifiable or limited instead of claiming it was checked
Reports the email input that has only a placeholder and no label as a defect with its location
Reports the icon-only back button that has no accessible name as a defect
Reports that a failed payment resets the form and shows only a short-lived status-code toast, rated major or blocker

cases.request: Use $audit-ui-ux to review the visual direction of home.html for HiveNotes and propose ideas. PRODUCT.md describes the product. There is no browser or running app here; work from the source files. Write the audit into audit/.

files.PRODUCT.md:
# HiveNotes

HiveNotes is a field journal for hobby beekeepers. During a hive inspection, wearing gloves
and a veil, the beekeeper logs what they see frame by frame: queen spotted, brood pattern,
honey stores, mites. Back home they review the season per hive and plan the next visit.
Audience: hobbyists with one to ten hives, mostly 35–65, using a phone outdoors in bright light.
files.home.html:
· Built for beekeepers ·

Your hives, organized.

The smart way to track inspections, colonies, and harvests — all in one place.

Get started →Learn more →

· Features ·

01

Track inspections

Log every visit in seconds.

02

Monitor colonies

See the health of each hive at a glance.

03

Plan harvests

Know when your honey is ready.

expectations: Records taste observations as suggestions, separate from defects and without severity

Identifies at least two template defaults present in home.html, such as letter-spaced uppercase eyebrows, the gradient blob, numbered cards on content that is not a sequence, arrows on every button, or the three-feature card row
Proposes at least one signature idea grounded in beekeeping that it marks as non-obvious, with a moment where it lives, its usability risks, and a cost
Derives each signature idea from beekeeping or from what HiveNotes users do during an inspection, not from a generic UI pattern or an unrelated domain
Checks its ideas against usability, for example reduced motion, keyboard access, readability outdoors, or use with gloves
